title: Establish customer-weighted intake lane with shadow-trial orchestration and pin-policy for enterprise models
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and ship a dedicated intake lane for enterprise-sourced model requests that weights customer criticality, orchestrates shadow trials/canaries, and applies a standardized pin-policy for production-serving. This playbook will be the canonical process for triaging new model onboarding, version pin requests, and scheduled deprecations originating from sales/CS.

Background:
Large customers frequently request model additions or version pins to preserve behavior for their products. Current intake is ad-hoc — requests land in general queues, causing unpredictable SLAs, inconsistent eval coverage, and manual adoptions that increase maintenance burden. We need a reproducible, auditable lane that reduces customer friction while protecting platform stability.

Goals:
- Provide a customer-weighted scoring rubric so high-value customers receive predictable SLAs and orchestrated validation steps.
- Automate shadow trial orchestration so customers can validate a model variant in production-like traffic without affecting global routing.
- Define a pin-policy template (timebox, review cadence, rollback criteria) for model versions requested by customers.
- Ensure eval gates (safety, perf, regression) are applied before any pin or canary roll.

Out of scope:
- New pricing/contract negotiation for pinned capacity (handled by Sales).
- Full automation of infra provisioning for every shadow trial (we will integrate with Dedicated capacity orchestration but not replace it).

Proposed solution:
1) Intake form enhancements: extend current intake form to capture customer tier, revenue signal, SLA expectation, and requested scope (model, variant, quantization). Add a field to indicate whether customer requests a temporary pin, permanent pin, or sunset exemption.
2) Scoring and lane assignment: compute a customer-weighted score using signals (ARR band, security requirements, compliance needs, latency SLO). Requests above a threshold route to the Enterprise Triage Lane (ETL) with a 10-business-day SLA for initial response.
3) Shadow trial orchestration: define runbooks for launching shadow trials: traffic sampling percentage, time window, success metrics (latency P95, token-cost delta, semantic-regression thresholds). Integrate with console to expose shadow metrics to CS and customer stakeholders.
4) Pin-policy template: default time-boxed pin (90 days), mandatory regression/eval checks at 30 and 75 days, automatic expiry with renewal flow. Provide clear rollback triggers and automated fallback to previous pinned variant.
5) Eval gates & audit: require structured eval suite (functional tests, safety checks, perf bench) linked in catalog entry prior to pin approval. All decisions logged in catalog and surfaced to compliance/audit.
6) Runbook + templates: ship a playbook with communication templates for CS/Sales, checklist for Eng to run canaries, and a dashboard card for monitoring active pins/shadow trials.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form updated and live in CS/Sales flow, capturing required fields.
- Score-based routing implemented in triage queuing with deterministic assignment to ETL.
- Shadow trial job template available in Console and can be launched by oncall/solutions eng within 1 business day.
- Pin-policy document published and adopted for new customer pin requests; automated expiry alerts generated.
- Eval gate checklist enforced: any pin must reference a catalog entry with passing perf and safety checks.

Success metrics:
- Mean time to first response for enterprise model requests <= 2 business days.
- Percentage of enterprise pins with a linked shadow trial >= 70% within first 3 months.
- Reduction in emergency rollbacks related to customer pins by 50% in quarter after launch.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Asha Patel (owner)
- Eng leads: Priya Narang (runtime), David Kim (catalog), Rachel Soto (console)
- Solutions/CS: Jasmine Ortiz
- Legal/Compliance: Marco Alvarez (advisory)
- Design: Ethan Brooks (communication templates)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Shadow trials could increase cost if left running; Mitigation: default sampling rates and TTLs, billing alerts.
- Risk: Poorly specified evals lead to false negatives; Mitigation: provide evaluation templates and require a steward owner for each catalog entry.
- Risk: Sales pressure to over-pin; Mitigation: time-box pins and require quarterly renewal with product sign-off.

Implementation tasks (high-level):
- PM: finalize scoring rubric and acceptance criteria.
- Design: update intake UI and CS templates.
- Eng (catalog): add metadata fields and pin state machine.
- Eng (console): shadow trial UI, shadow metrics dashboard, and alerts.
- Eng (runtime): automated fallback for pinned variants and canary routing hooks.
- Legal/Compliance: review audit logging requirements.

Links & artifacts:
- Intake prototype doc: https://docs.company.com/model-catalog/enterprise-intake-proto (confluence)
- Eval templates: https://drive.company.com/open?id=eval-templates-2025
- Reference PR for catalog metadata: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/482

Notes:
This playbook emphasizes deterministic treatment of enterprise requests and reduces ad-hoc exceptions. The lane should be extensible (fast-track options for trusted partners) and provide clear signals back to Sales/CS when a request cannot be satisfied within platform constraints.
